title: Group Chat and Recipe
premise: Mirabel Villalobos has spent a decade perfecting the art of being overlooked, tracking every statistic at Hollow Creek High while never appearing in any of them. When the school's legendary ghost — tied to a century-old recipe that founded the town's cannery fortune — begins leaving her handwritten notes in ink that shouldn't exist, she learns the 'ghost' is a dying tradition itself: an entity sustained by the annual Founders' Feast, and this year no one remembers to feed it. As Mirabel uncovers how the town's founding families rigged the recipe's legacy to erase the immigrant workers who actually created it, she realizes the ghost is one of those erased ancestors, and saving it means exposing the lie her own family helped bury. In the end, Mirabel chooses visibility over survival-by-invisibility, publicly restoring the true recipe and the names behind it — which frees the ghost but costs Mirabel her careful anonymity forever.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper archivist who spent years cataloguing faded recipes and obituaries from mill towns across the Midwest. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who discover their towns are built on secrets.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Counts Everything
chapters.summary: Mirabel Villalobos, POV. Opening on game night, Mirabel tracks statistics from the bleachers, invisible by design, cataloguing the school's rituals with obsessive precision. We learn her rule: be so careful it hurts, and nothing can hurt you. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: Note One
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. She finds a note tucked into her stats binder: 'You see the pattern, Mirabel.' The ink is deep violet and slightly warm, impossible under the fluorescent lights. No one knows her name here. Emotional beat: terror and a shameful thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: Group Chat: 11:47 PM
chapters.summary: Alternating texts among Mirabel, her estranged ex-best-friend Priya, and jock Theo as someone screenshots the note into the class group chat. Rumors of the Hollow Creek Ghost ignite. Mirabel lies badly about knowing anything. Emotional beat: panic as invisibility cracks.

chapters.title: What the Town Eats
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Researching in the library basement, she finds the Founders' Feast tradition: every October, the town recreates the Villalobos Cannery's legendary recipe. Her own surname is on the plaque, but the details are wrong. Emotional beat: unease at a history that doesn't add up.

chapters.title: Note Two: A Recipe Card
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. A second note appears inside her locker — an old recipe card in the same impossible ink, half a list, addressed again by name. When she touches it, she hears faint canning-line sounds. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Priya Remembers
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya recalls why she and Mirabel stopped speaking: three years ago Mirabel stayed silent when Priya was blamed for something. Priya sees the notes as Mirabel finally asking for help — or finally owing one. Emotional beat: resentment with buried tenderness.

chapters.title: The Statistician's Proof
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Applying statistical analysis to town archives, Mirabel proves the Feast recipe was altered in 1934 — the same year eleven cannery workers' names vanish from all records. Emotional beat: the intoxication of a pattern finally visible.

chapters.title: Theo's Family Secret
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo admits his family are founding descendants; his grandmother made him swear never to ask about the cellar room. He's been leaving flowers there since he was six. He joins Mirabel reluctantly. Emotional beat: inherited guilt meeting curiosity.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Chemistry teacher Ms. Okafor tests the ink: no known compound, dated by oxidation to roughly ninety years old yet still wet. Something is writing across time. Emotional beat: rational worldview buckling.

chapters.title: Note Three: Hurry
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. The third note reads only 'HURRY' and lists a date — the night before this year's Feast. The ghost is fading; the notes are getting fainter. Mirabel feels time compressing around her. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Cellar Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel, Theo, and reluctant Priya break into the founders' cellar. They find a wall of erased names beneath whitewash, and the original recipe — written by a woman named Esperanza Villalobos, Mirabel's ancestor. Emotional beat: awe and betrayal entwined.

chapters.title: Rigged
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Archival cross-referencing reveals the founding families stole Esperanza's recipe, credited themselves, and struck the workers from record when they demanded wages. Mirabel's own line survived by staying quiet. Emotional beat: horror at complicity in her bloodline.

chapters.title: Group Chat Fracture
chapters.summary: Group chat scene. Screenshots of the cellar leak; the town splits between those demanding the truth and founding families threatening expulsion and lawsuits. Theo wavers under family pressure. Emotional beat: belonging tested by loyalty.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Was Careful About
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Flashback chapter: ten years ago, young Mirabel learned that speaking up got people hurt — her father lost work after testifying about unsafe conditions. Silence became armor. Emotional beat: compassion for her own fear.

chapters.title: Esperanza Speaks
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. In the cellar at dusk, the ghost manifests: not a monster but Esperanza, sustained for a century by the Feast's echo of her cooking, now starving because the altered recipe no longer carries her. She asks Mirabel to cook the true recipe, publicly, in her name. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya confronts Mirabel: doing this means exposure, retaliation, maybe worse — everything Mirabel spent a decade avoiding. Priya offers to stand beside her anyway. Old friendship rekindles through honesty. Emotional beat: reconciliation.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The founding families lock the Feast kitchen and destroy the recovered recipe card. Theo must choose: his grandmother's threats or his friends. He photographs the originals hidden in the cellar wall and sends them to the group chat. Emotional beat: courage breaking lineage.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Countdown structure: the trio reconstructs the recipe from Mirabel's statistical memory, Priya's grandmother's oral versions, and Theo's family records. The ghost's ink fades page by page. Emotional beat: desperate, collaborative hope.

chapters.title: The Feast
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV (climax). At the Founders' Feast, Mirabel walks onstage — visible, terrified, named — and cooks Esperanza's recipe before the whole town, reading the erased eleven names aloud as the smell fills the hall. The founding families' objections drown in collective memory. Emotional beat: triumph through vulnerability.

chapters.title: What the Ink Was For
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Esperanza appears one last time, solid now, and thanks her: the notes were never haunting, but a hand reaching for anyone careful enough to notice patterns. She dissolves into ordinary morning light. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Aftermath, By the Numbers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via group chat and news excerpts. The town renames the Feast; the eleven names go on the plaque; investigations begin. Mirabel faces social fallout but also unexpected belonging — people keep finding her to tell her their family's erased stories. Emotional beat: cost acknowledged, worth affirmed.

chapters.title: Recipe for the Next One
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Epilogue: Mirabel writes her own note in ordinary blue ink and leaves it in the stats binder for whoever comes next — a shy freshman who counts everything. Final line mirrors the first note: 'You see the pattern.' Emotional beat: inheritance, chosen freely.
